subject: Acelabs: Request for key custody evidence and TLS binding details
participants_external: jane.dobson@acelabs.com (Jane Dobson, Head of Cloud Security)
messages:
From: Jane Dobson <jane.dobson@acelabs.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: security@acelabs.com, procurement@acelabs.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Key custody evidence + TLS binding details required for procurement

Rishi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and our cloud security teams are moving this RFP to the final evaluation stage and we need a concise packet of evidence for key custody and TLS binding to complete our risk acceptance review. Specifically we need:  

- A diagram and narrative describing BYOK import flow (customer key material -> HSM or KMS vault) including any manual steps.
- Evidence of HSM attestation options (vendor, model, attestation tokens).
- TLS mutual-auth and cipher suites supported for customer-facing endpoints; we also want mTLS for key management control plane where possible.
- Key rotation window recommendations and how rotation impacts in-flight sessions / KV cache.
- Export/import procedures: what forms of key export are supported and any escrow options.

Can you deliver a single packet (PDF preferred) with the above plus any attachments (certs, test vectors) by EOD today? Also let us know if you anticipate any gaps we should raise now.

Best,
Jane
Jane Dobson
Head of Cloud Security, Acelabs

Hi Jane —

Thanks, we can do that. I'll assemble the packet and include artifacts for HSM attestation and the TLS cipher matrix. Two quick clarifications to ensure we deliver the exact evidence you expect:  

1) For "HSM attestation tokens" — do you need vendor-signed attestation (e.g., AWS Nitro Enclaves / CloudHSM attestation statements) or table-level evidence listing supported FIPS/CC certifications?
2) For "export/import procedures" — are you evaluating (a) customer-generated key import via wrapped blobs (BYOK), (b) remote escrow via partner, or (c) physical HSM courier-based handoff? We support multiple flows; want to prioritize.

If you confirm by 10:30 PT we'll target a consolidated PDF and separate CSV of cipher suites.

- Rishi
VP of Product Security
Redwood Inference

Folks — forwarding Acelabs' request (see below). They want a single packet with BYOK flow, HSM attestation options, TLS/mTLS cipher matrix, rotation guidance, and export/import procedures. Need this by EOD their time (same day). Can you please:  

- Priyom: draft the BYOK import flow diagram + step-by-step import/export procedures; include wrapped-blob example (KMS envelope) and note supported key formats and wrapping ciphers. Also list HSM models we integrate with and attestation capabilities.
- Marissa: assemble TLS matrix (endpoint types, supported ciphers, mTLS options), and write the rotation section — include recommended rotation windows, KV cache invalidation behavior, and rollback guidance for canaryed model rollouts.

I'll review and add procurement-facing narrative. Attachments to include: redwood_kms_byo_faq.pdf (compiled answers), tls_cipher_matrix.csv, rotation_playbook_v1.docx. Keep answers concise — bullet lists are fine.

Thanks — can you get drafts in 60–90 mins?

Rishi

From: priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: FW: Key custody evidence + TLS binding details required for procurement

Rishi / Marissa — draft attached below. High-level summary and bullet answers; added attachment stubs.

Attachment stubs included in packet:  
- redwood_kms_byo_faq.pdf (contains BYOK import example, wrapped-blob sample, and attestation table)
- tls_cipher_matrix.csv (endpoint,type,ciphers,mTLS_supported)
- rotation_playbook_v1.docx (operator runbook for key rotation and KV cache handling)

Draft excerpts (for the packet):

BYOK import flow (summary):
1) Customer generates an asymmetric or symmetric key locally (recommended RSA-3072 or AES-256-GCM keywrap).
2) Customer creates a key-encryption-key (KEK) and wraps the key material per our supported envelope format (RFC 7516-like envelope; we provide a client helper for AWS KMS/Wrapping).
3) Wrapped key blob is uploaded via the Private control plane (VPC peering or SFTP for air-gapped customers) to the Redwood import service.
4) Import service verifies signature and stores the unwrapped key inside an HSM-backed vault or dedicated KMS partition. Unwrapped keys are never persisted outside HSM boundary.

HSM attestation & models:
- We support integration with AWS CloudHSM (nCipher/Thales on partner-managed HSMs), AWS Nitro enclaves-based attestation, and on-prem Thales Luna.
- Attestation: we can provide vendor-signed attestation statements and TPM-like measurement logs where available. For CloudHSM, we provide device serials and PKCS#11 token info as evidence; for dedicated HSMs we supply cert chains and firmware/OS versions.

Export/import and escrow:
- Direct key export (cleartext) from our HSM is not permitted except during customer-authorized maintenance windows and only under dual-control.
- Supported export methods: wrapped-blob export (customer-wrapped), HSM-to-HSM secure key transfer (mutual attestation & encrypted channel), and documented escrow via partner (separate contract).

Rotation and in-flight sessions:
- Recommended rotation window: 90–180 days for KEKs, 365+ days for master-signing keys depending on workload risk profile.
- Rolling rotation is supported: new key is staged, cache TTLs honored, and we maintain both old/new key-material for a configurable overlap period (default 24 hours) to reduce failed in-flight requests. KV cache entries are versioned; mismatches return structured 429/410 with retry guidance.

I'll attach the full packet (PDF + CSV + DOCX) once Marissa confirms the TLS table.

— Priyom
Principal, Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>

Cc: procurement@acelabs.com, security@acelabs.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Key custody evidence + TLS binding details required for procurement

Jane —

Thanks for the clear ask. Attached is a single packet that should cover your reviewers: redwood_kms_byo_faq.pdf (BYOK flows, attestation evidence index, wrapped-blob example), tls_cipher_matrix.csv (endpoint-level cipher/mTLS support), and rotation_playbook_v1.docx (operator runbook and rollback guidance).  

Quick highlights:  
- BYOK import: we accept customer-wrapped blobs (AES-256-GCM or RSA-OAEP-4096 wrapping). Unwrapped keys are injected directly into HSM vaults; we do not retain cleartext outside the HSM boundary.
- Attestation: where supported by the hardware/cloud provider, we can supply vendor-signed attestation tokens and device cert chains. For private deployments we provide firmware/serial evidence and signed measurement logs.
- TLS/mTLS: all control-plane endpoints support TLS1.2+; recommended minimum TLS1.3 for customer-facing inference endpoints. mTLS is supported on the Key Management API for Private deployments and on Dedicated via customer-configured VPNs. See attached CSV for exact ciphers per endpoint.
- Rotation: default overlap window is 24 hours; we keep previous key-material for staged rollouts. For critical workloads we recommend KEK rotation every 90 days and a planned rewrap cadence for derived keys.

Open items for your team to confirm (so we can finalize legal/ops artifacts):  
1) Preferred attestation artifacts (vendor tokens vs certification lists).
2) Channel for transfer of wrapped blobs (SFTP vs private control-plane upload).
3) Any escrow/legalese required for partner-managed escrow (we have templated options).

If that looks good, we can schedule a 30-minute session to walk security through the packet tomorrow morning.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Product Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_kms_byo_faq.pdf (PDF), tls_cipher_matrix.csv (CSV), rotation_playbook_v1.docx (DOCX)
